subject: RetailFlux renewal: hosted commit uplift + new rate bands
messages:
From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@retailflux.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-11-05T09:14:00-08:00
Subject: Hosted commit increase — quick numbers and timing

Hi Jordan,

Quick note from my side: RetailFlux is planning a major marketing push in Q1 and we expect a ~3.5x spike in hosted API usage for inference calls (text generation + embeddings). We're interested in moving from our current 1.2M token/month committed plan to something in the 4–5M token/month range with predictable rate bands and a modest price break for higher commit.

Can you share an initial pricing sketch and any SIMD/burst guidance? Also need to understand the invoicing cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and whether we can keep the soft throttle we agreed on last year for overflow.

Asha (copied) will coordinate procurement. We're hoping for an uplift that starts by Jan 1, 2026.

Thanks,
Jordan Lee
Head of Platform, RetailFlux

RetailFlux (retailflux.com)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Hosted commit increase — quick numbers and timing

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the heads up and timing.

High level: we can support a jump to 4–5M committed tokens/month with two practical levers: a) a tiered unit price that decreases at higher commit bands, and b) an expanded burst pocket for seasonal spikes (configurable and limited to percentage of commit). We typically recommend a 10–15% burst buffer on top of the committed band for marketing spikes, plus prefix caching for repeated prompts which will reduce billable tokens.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben will draft a rate schedule and show optics for 4M vs 5M commits.
- Monica will scope any SLA or invoice cadence changes and confirm the soft-throttle behavior during spikes.
- We can schedule a 30-min call this week to walk through the workbook.

Can you confirm the preferred invoicing cadence (monthly/quarterly) and whether you want a calendar-aligned start (Jan 1) or a rolling 30-day post-signature start?

Jordan B.
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Subject: RetailFlux proposed rate schedule and uplift scenarios (draft)

Jordan / Monica — attaching a draft rate schedule and uplift SOW for RetailFlux. Summary of scenarios:

1) 4M commitment/month
   - Unit price: $0.00090 per token (hosted gen tier)
   - Burst pocket: 12% monthly burst (auto-bucket), overage billed at $0.00105/token
   - Invoice: monthly, net 30

2) 5M commitment/month (recommended for marketing push)
   - Unit price: $0.00082 per token
   - Burst pocket: 15% monthly burst, overage billed at $0.00098/token
   - Invoice: monthly or quarterly (quarterly gives a 1.5% discount on charges)

Assumptions: 70% of traffic is generation, 30% embeddings; prefix caching expected to reduce billable gen tokens by ~8–12% for repeated prompts.

Attachments: retailflux_proposed_rate_schedule.xlsx (pricing bands + sample invoice), redwood_uplift-sow.pdf (ops runbook + rollback plan).

Thanks Ben — that looks reasonable. A few asks from our side before we route to procurement:

- Can Redwood add a short SLA note for latency for the 5M commit band? Our ops team needs a baseline for P95 inference latency during marketing windows.
- We prefer quarterly invoicing (gives us simpler forecasting). You mentioned a small discount — can you put that percentage on the table so our finance team can approve quickly?
- We also need a short SOC2 addendum and confirmation of audit log retention (12 months minimum).

Tom (copied) is the approver for spend >$200k ARR. If you can provide the updated SOW + a DocuSign link for signature, we'll aim to sign before Dec 15 to hit Jan 1 start.

Best,
Jordan

Subject: Action items & updated commercial terms for RetailFlux uplift

Jordan / team — thanks for the quick reviews. Summary of agreed updates and next steps (operational + commercial):

1) Commercial terms (final):
   - Selected: 5M tokens/month committed
   - Unit price: $0.00082/token (as proposed)
   - Quarterly invoicing (net 45) with 1.5% quarterly prepay discount if RetailFlux elects calendar-quarter prepayment
   - DocuSign: we'll generate final SOW and commercial exhibit and share a signing link by 11/14.

2) Operational / SLA notes:
   - P95 latency target for the 5M band: 200–250ms for generation workloads on hosted clusters in us-west-2, subject to model/seq-length mix; we'll publish the per-route baseline in the Console prior to go-live.
   - Burst pocket: 15% monthly auto-bucket; overage priced at $0.00098/token. Bursts beyond 40% sustained for >6 hours trigger soft throttle; we'll notify and coordinate scale-up.
   - Audit logs & retention: 12 months retention via Private Customer Audit Feed; SOC2 addendum attached.

3) Ramp and go-live:
   - Goal start: 2026-01-01 (calendar-aligned) pending signed SOW.
   - Canary: 2-week progressive ramp (10% -> 40% -> 100%) with log-based quality gates; ops pager to be on-call first week.

4) Action owners & deadlines:
   - Ben: finalize pricing workbook and attach sample invoice (due 11/14).
   - Jordan B: push DocuSign and run internal discount approval for 1.5% prepay option (due 11/14).
   - Jordan L / Tom: confirm signature authority and notify procurement about SOC2 addendum (target sign by 12/15).

Attachments included in final send: redwood_uplift-sow.pdf; retailflux_proposed_rate_schedule.xlsx (sample).
